    10	  "goal": [
    11	    {
    12	      "id": "fintech-vs-traditional-crossover",
    13	      "insight": "Visually contrast the rising trajectory of digital payment penetration and digital bank licenses against the declining trajectory of traditional bank branches, making the crossover dynamics prominent"
    14	    },
    15	    {
    16	      "id": "branch-decline-acceleration",
    17	      "insight": "Emphasize the significant pace of traditional bank branch closures, highlighting the sharp acceleration from 2019 to 2020 and the sustained high rate of closures since then"
    18	    },
    19	    {
    20	      "id": "neobank-user-surge",
    21	      "insight": "Highlight the explosive growth in neobank user counts across major markets, showing which regions lead adoption"
    22	    },
    23	    {
    24	      "id": "regulatory-license-wave",
    25	      "insight": "Show the temporal pattern of digital banking license approvals across regions, emphasizing the clustering of approvals in certain years"
    26	    },
    27	    {
    28	      "id": "regional-disparity",
    29	      "insight": "Compare the pace of fintech disruption across regions (North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America), making geographic differences in adoption and displacement visually clear"
    30	    }
    31	  ]
    32	}

     3	## Overview
     4	Four datasets tracking the global shift from traditional banking to fintech-driven digital finance across four regions (North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America) over a ten-year period from 2015 to 2024.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### digital_payment_penetration
     9	Annual digital payment adoption rate as a percentage of the adult population. Fields: `year` (integer, 2015–2024), `region` (string, 4 categories), `penetration_pct` (float, 18.3–91.2%). Represents share of adults who made at least one digital payment transaction in the year.
    10	
    11	### traditional_bank_branches
    12	Total number of physical bank branch locations in thousands. Fields: `year` (integer, 2015–2024), `region` (string, 4 categories), `branches_k` (float, 58.6–315.8 thousand). Covers commercial and retail bank branches.
    13	
    14	### neobank_users
    15	Cumulative registered users of digital-only banks (neobanks) in millions. Fields: `year` (integer, 2016–2024), `region` (string, 4 categories), `users_m` (float, 0.8–498.3 million). Starts from 2016 when neobanks began gaining traction.
    16	
    17	### digital_bank_licenses
    18	Cumulative count of full digital banking licenses approved by national regulators. Fields: `year` (integer, 2015–2024), `region` (string, 4 categories), `cumulative_licenses` (integer, 0–85).
    19	
    20	## Data Notes
    21	- All figures are estimated composites across countries within each region
    22	- Digital payment penetration includes mobile wallets, online banking transfers, and contactless card payments
    23	- Neobank user counts include registered accounts; active user rates vary by region
    24	- License counts reflect full banking licenses only, excluding e-money or payment institution licenses
    25	- The 2020 spike in digital adoption reflects pandemic-accelerated behavioral shifts

     7	# Data Visualization Skill
     8	
     9	Chart selection guidance, Python visualization code patterns, design principles, and accessibility considerations for creating effective data visualizations.
    10	
    11	## Chart Selection Guide
    12	
    13	### Choose by Data Relationship
    14	
    15	| What You're Showing | Best Chart | Alternatives |
    16	|---|---|---|
    17	| **Trend over time** | Line chart | Area chart (if showing cumulative or composition) |
    18	| **Comparison across categories** | Vertical bar chart | Horizontal bar (many categories), lollipop chart |
    19	| **Ranking** | Horizontal bar chart | Dot plot, slope chart (comparing two periods) |
    20	| **Part-to-whole composition** | Stacked bar chart | Treemap (hierarchical), waffle chart |
    21	| **Composition over time** | Stacked area chart | 100% stacked bar (for proportion focus) |
    22	| **Distribution** | Histogram | Box plot (comparing groups), violin plot, strip plot |
    23	| **Correlation (2 variables)** | Scatter plot | Bubble chart (add 3rd variable as size) |
    24	| **Correlation (many variables)** | Heatmap (correlation matrix) | Pair plot |
    25	| **Geographic patterns** | Choropleth map | Bubble map, hex map |
    26	| **Flow / process** | Sankey diagram | Funnel chart (sequential stages) |
    27	| **Relationship network** | Network graph | Chord diagram |
    28	| **Performance vs. target** | Bullet chart | Gauge (single KPI only) |
    29	| **Multiple KPIs at once** | Small multiples | Dashboard with separate charts |
    30	
    31	### When NOT to Use Certain Charts
    32	
    33	- **Pie charts**: Avoid unless <6 categories and exact proportions matter less than rough comparison. Humans are bad at comparing angles. Use bar charts instead.
    34	- **3D charts**: Never. They distort perception and add no information.
    35	- **Dual-axis charts**: Use cautiously. They can mislead by implying correlation. Clearly label both axes if used.
    36	- **Stacked bar (many categories)**: Hard to compare middle segments. Use small multiples or grouped bars instead.
    37	- **Donut charts**: Slightly better than pie charts but same fundamental issues. Use for single KPI display at most.
    38	
    39	## Python Visualization Code Patterns
    40

   192	def format_number(val, format_type='number'):
   193	    """Format numbers for chart labels."""
   194	    if format_type == 'currency':
   195	        if abs(val) >= 1e9:
   196	            return f'${val/1e9:.1f}B'
   197	        elif abs(val) >= 1e6:
   198	            return f'${val/1e6:.1f}M'
   199	        elif abs(val) >= 1e3:
   200	            return f'${val/1e3:.1f}K'
   201	        else:
   202	            return f'${val:,.0f}'
   203	    elif format_type == 'percent':
   204	        return f'{val:.1f}%'
   205	    elif format_type == 'number':
   206	        if abs(val) >= 1e9:
   207	            return f'{val/1e9:.1f}B'
   208	        elif abs(val) >= 1e6:
   209	            return f'{val/1e6:.1f}M'
   210	        elif abs(val) >= 1e3:

   240	
   241	## Design Principles
   242	
   243	### Color
   244	
   245	- **Use color purposefully**: Color should encode data, not decorate
   246	- **Highlight the story**: Use a bright accent color for the key insight; grey everything else
   247	- **Sequential data**: Use a single-hue gradient (light to dark) for ordered values
   248	- **Diverging data**: Use a two-hue gradient with neutral midpoint for data with a meaningful center
   249	- **Categorical data**: Use distinct hues, maximum 6-8 before it gets confusing
   250	- **Avoid red/green only**: 8% of men are red-green colorblind. Use blue/orange as primary pair
   251	
   252	### Typography
   253	
   254	- **Title states the insight**: "Revenue grew 23% YoY" beats "Revenue by Month"
   255	- **Subtitle adds context**: Date range, filters applied, data source
   256	- **Axis labels are readable**: Never rotated 90 degrees if avoidable. Shorten or wrap instead
   257	- **Data labels add precision**: Use on key points, not every single bar
   258	- **Annotation highlights**: Call out specific points with text annotations
   259	
   260	### Layout
   261	
   262	- **Reduce chart junk**: Remove gridlines, borders, backgrounds that don't carry information
   263	- **Sort meaningfully**: Categories sorted by value (not alphabetically) unless there's a natural order (months, stages)
   264	- **Appropriate aspect ratio**: Time series wider than tall (3:1 to 2:1); comparisons can be squarer
   265	- **White space is good**: Don't cram charts together. Give each visualization room to breathe
   266	
   267	### Accuracy
   268	
   269	- **Bar charts start at zero**: Always. A bar from 95 to 100 exaggerates a 5% difference
   270	- **Line charts can have non-zero baselines**: When the range of variation is meaningful
   271	- **Consistent scales across panels**: When comparing multiple charts, use the same axis range
   272	- **Show uncertainty**: Error bars, confidence intervals, or ranges when data is uncertain
   273	- **Label your axes**: Never make the reader guess what the numbers mean
   274	
   275	## Accessibility Considerations
   276	
   277	### Color Blindness
   278	
   279	- Never rely on color alone to distinguish data series
   280	- Add pattern fills, different line styles (solid, dashed, dotted), or direct labels
   281	- Test with a colorblind simulator (e.g., Coblis, Sim Daltonism)
   282	- Use the colorblind-friendly palette: `sns.color_palette("colorblind")`
   283	
   284	### Screen Readers
   285	
   286	- Include alt text describing the chart's key finding
   287	- Provide a data table alternative alongside the visualization
   288	- Use semantic titles and labels
   289	
   290	### General Accessibility
   291	
   292	- Sufficient contrast between data elements and background
   293	- Text size minimum 10pt for labels, 12pt for titles
   294	- Avoid conveying information only through spatial position (add labels)
   295	- Consider printing: does the chart work in black and white?
   296	
   297	### Accessibility Checklist
   298	
   299	Before sharing a visualization:
   300	- [ ] Chart works without color (patterns, labels, or line styles differentiate series)
   301	- [ ] Text is readable at standard zoom level
   302	- [ ] Title describes the insight, not just the data
   303	- [ ] Axes are labeled with units
   304	- [ ] Legend is clear and positioned without obscuring data
   305	- [ ] Data source and date range are noted

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import json

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Convert to DataFrames
df_payments = pd.DataFrame(data['digital_payment_penetration']['data'])
df_branches = pd.DataFrame(data['traditional_bank_branches']['data'])
df_neo = pd.DataFrame(data['neobank_users']['data'])
df_licenses = pd.DataFrame(data['digital_bank_licenses']['data'])

# Professional business/executive style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.dpi': 200,
    'font.size': 10,
    'axes.titlesize': 12,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 10,
    'xtick.labelsize': 9,
    'ytick.labelsize': 9,
    'legend.fontsize': 9,
    'figure.titlesize': 14,
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
})

# Color palette - professional, colorblind-friendly
regions = ['North America', 'Europe', 'Asia-Pacific', 'Latin America']
colors = {
    'North America': '#1f4e79',
    'Europe': '#c55a11',
    'Asia-Pacific': '#548235',
    'Latin America': '#7030a0',
}

# Create 2x2 layout
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))
fig.patch.set_facecolor('white')

# ===================== Panel 1: Crossover Dynamics (Top-Left) =====================
ax1 = axes[0, 0]

# Global averages for crossover story
global_payments = df_payments.groupby('year')['penetration_pct'].mean().reset_index()
global_branches = df_branches.groupby('year')['branches_k'].sum().reset_index()

# Normalize branches to 2015 = 100 for visual comparison
branch_base = global_branches['branches_k'].iloc[0]
global_branches['branches_index'] = (global_branches['branches_k'] / branch_base) * 100

# Plot payment penetration on left axis
ax1_twin = ax1.twinx()
line1 = ax1.plot(global_payments['year'], global_payments['penetration_pct'],
                 color='#1f4e79', linewidth=3, marker='o', markersize=6,
                 label='Digital Payment Penetration (%)')
ax1.set_ylabel('Digital Payment Penetration (%)', color='#1f4e79', fontweight='bold')
ax1.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#1f4e79')
ax1.set_ylim(0, 100)

# Plot branch index on right axis
line2 = ax1_twin.plot(global_branches['year'], global_branches['branches_index'],
                      color='#c55a11', linewidth=3, marker='s', markersize=6,
                      linestyle='--', label='Traditional Bank Branches (Indexed)')
ax1_twin.set_ylabel('Traditional Branches (2015 = 100)', color='#c55a11', fontweight='bold')
ax1_twin.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#c55a11')
ax1_twin.set_ylim(60, 110)

# Add crossover annotation around 2020
ax1.annotate('Pandemic Acceleration\n(2020)', xy=(2020, 65), xytext=(2017, 82),
            fontsize=9, ha='center',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='black', lw=1.2),
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#f2f2f2', edgecolor='gray'))

ax1.set_xlabel('Year')
ax1.set_title('The Crossover: Digital Rise vs. Physical Decline', fontweight='bold', fontsize=12)
ax1.set_xticks(range(2015, 2025, 2))

# Combined legend
lines = line1 + line2
labels = [l.get_label() for l in lines]
ax1.legend(lines, labels, loc='center left', frameon=True, fontsize=8)

ax1.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax1_twin.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

# ===================== Panel 2: Branch Decline by Region (Top-Right) =====================
ax2 = axes[0, 1]

for region in regions:
    subset = df_branches[df_branches['region'] == region]
    ax2.plot(subset['year'], subset['branches_k'], color=colors[region],
             linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=5, label=region)

# Highlight 2019-2020 acceleration with shaded region
ax2.axvspan(2019, 2020, alpha=0.15, color='red', label='2019-2020 Shock')

# Annotation for sharp drop
ax2.annotate('Sharp Acceleration\nin Branch Closures', xy=(2020, 250), xytext=(2017.5, 290),
            fontsize=9, ha='center',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='black', lw=1.2),
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#f2f2f2', edgecolor='gray'))

ax2.set_xlabel('Year')
ax2.set_ylabel('Bank Branches (thousands)')
ax2.set_title('Traditional Branch Decline Accelerates Post-2019', fontweight='bold', fontsize=12)
ax2.set_xticks(range(2015, 2025, 2))
ax2.legend(loc='upper right', frameon=True, fontsize=8)
ax2.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax2.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# ===================== Panel 3: Neobank User Surge (Bottom-Left) =====================
ax3 = axes[1, 0]

for region in regions:
    subset = df_neo[df_neo['region'] == region]
    ax3.fill_between(subset['year'], subset['users_m'], alpha=0.2, color=colors[region])
    ax3.plot(subset['year'], subset['users_m'], color=colors[region],
             linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=5, label=region)

# Annotation for Asia-Pacific leadership
ap_max = df_neo[df_neo['region'] == 'Asia-Pacific']['users_m'].max()
ax3.annotate('Asia-Pacific Leads\n(498M users in 2024)', xy=(2024, 498), xytext=(2021.5, 420),
            fontsize=9, ha='center',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#548235', lw=1.2),
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#e2efd9', edgecolor='#548235'))

ax3.set_xlabel('Year')
ax3.set_ylabel('Neobank Users (millions)')
ax3.set_title('Explosive Neobank User Growth by Region', fontweight='bold', fontsize=12)
ax3.set_xticks(range(2016, 2025, 2))
ax3.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, fontsize=8)
ax3.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax3.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# ===================== Panel 4: License Approvals (Bottom-Right) =====================
ax4 = axes[1, 1]

# Compute annual new licenses from cumulative
df_licenses_sorted = df_licenses.sort_values(['region', 'year'])
df_licenses_sorted['new_licenses'] = df_licenses_sorted.groupby('region')['cumulative_licenses'].diff().fillna(df_licenses_sorted['cumulative_licenses'])

# Stacked bar for new licenses by year
pivot_licenses = df_licenses_sorted.pivot(index='year', columns='region', values='new_licenses').fillna(0)
pivot_licenses = pivot_licenses[regions]  # order

bottom = np.zeros(len(pivot_licenses))
bars_list = []
for region in regions:
    bars = ax4.bar(pivot_licenses.index, pivot_licenses[region], bottom=bottom,
                   color=colors[region], label=region, width=0.7, alpha=0.85)
    bars_list.append(bars)
    bottom += pivot_licenses[region].values

# Add total labels on top of bars
for i, year in enumerate(pivot_licenses.index):
    total = bottom[i]
    ax4.text(year, total + 1, f'{int(total)}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold')

# Highlight clustering years
ax4.axvspan(2019.5, 2021.5, alpha=0.1, color='green', label='License Wave')

ax4.set_xlabel('Year')
ax4.set_ylabel('New Digital Banking Licenses')
ax4.set_title('Regulatory License Waves Cluster in 2019-2021', fontweight='bold', fontsize=12)
ax4.set_xticks(range(2015, 2025, 1))
ax4.set_xticklabels([str(y) for y in range(2015, 2025)], rotation=45, ha='right')
ax4.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, fontsize=8)
ax4.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax4.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# ===================== Final Layout =====================
fig.suptitle('Fintech Disruption: Traditional Banking vs. Digital Finance (2015-2024)',
             fontsize=15, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)

# Add data source note
fig.text(0.5, 0.01, 'Source: Estimated composite data across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America',
         ha='center', fontsize=8, style='italic', color='gray')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
plt.close()
